eligibility.exact_action_basis: H.R. 192 would require Amtrak to make its annual operations report public on its website and replace the existing officer-pay item with disclosure of annual base pay and any bonus compensation paid to its executive leadership team, including the chief executive officer, president and officers, with the criteria and metrics used to determine bonuses. The existing report is due to Congress by February 15 each year; its prior paragraph (2) requires relevant information about a decision to pay an officer above Executive Schedule level I. The proposal changes that reporting item and adds website publication; it does not create the annual reporting duty from scratch or cap executive compensation. This is the January 13 suspension-and-passage choice on the whole bill.

H.R. 901 would add a duty to develop, with appropriate agency officials, a Department-wide policy and process protecting sensitive information in DHS research-and-development acquisitions against unauthorized access or disclosure. It would require a GAO report within one year after enactment on DHS compliance with NSPM-33 and adoption of the National Science and Technology Council's 2022 guidance, covering disclosures, reporting violations to relevant agencies, interagency guidelines and the Science and Technology Directorate's framework role. The Secretary must brief the two named homeland-security committees within 90 days on development of the safeguard policies/processes. The March 10 floor and EH both print the added duty as paragraph (15). The 2024 Code already has paragraph (15), added December 23, 2024 for drug-detection equipment/reference-library research. Existing paragraphs (13)/(14) also already have the punctuation resulting from that 2024 addition: paragraph (13) ends with a semicolon without the printed and that this bill directs stricken, and paragraph (14) ends with a semicolon and and rather than the period this bill directs replaced. This candidate preserves those amendment-instruction mismatches and the duplicate numbering; it does not infer replacement, renumbering or a definitive legal application.

H.R. 1534 would add an Energy Department program for research, development, demonstration and commercial application of advanced production and use of low-emissions cement, concrete and asphalt. Within 180 days after enactment, the Secretary must establish the program and support collaborative demonstrations; a five-year strategic plan is due within 180 days after program establishment and updated at least every two years. Advanced production requires at least one specified improvement in cost-effectiveness, quality/performance/resilience, or resource/material efficiency; low-emissions products must reduce greenhouse gases or directly related copollutants below commercially available products to the maximum practicable extent. Focus areas include carbon capture, heat, resource efficiency, computing, sensors, retrofits, data and materials science. Demonstration selection must, to the maximum practicable extent, encourage regional/rural and technological diversity, expand existing demonstrations, use achieved greenhouse-gas reductions and prioritize non-Federal matching funds. Reporting is at least biennial; the Secretary may terminate demonstrations upon the specified sufficient domestic commercial availability at comparable price. Technical assistance covers codes/standards data, life-cycle and environmental/techno-economic comparisons, permitting and testing, with competitive applications at least annually and optional regional centers. The Secretary must consider existing Manufacturing USA resources, integration and assistance consistent with its incorporated law, and coordinate with other agencies. The new section sunsets seven years after enactment, applies consistently with the named 2022 research-security subtitle and preserves the Secretary's environmental-industry-standard authority. It is a research/deployment-support proposal, not a mandate to buy particular materials or a finding that its economic/emissions goals will occur.

S.146 would insert a new223(h) for authentic intimate depictions and digital forgeries published knowingly through an interactive computer service in interstate or foreign commerce. Adult authentic-image liability requires knowledge or reasonable-knowledge of the specified reasonable expectation of privacy, that the depicted content was not voluntarily exposed by the individual in a public or commercial setting, that it is not a matter of public concern, and intended or actual harm. Adult digital-forgery liability instead expressly requires lack of consent, that the depicted content was not voluntarily exposed by the individual in a public or commercial setting, that it is not a matter of public concern, and intended or actual harm. For minors, each publication offense requires the specified intent to abuse, humiliate, harass or degrade, or to arouse or gratify sexual desire. A digital forgery must meet the bill's identifiable-person and reasonable-viewer indistinguishability-when-viewed-as-a-whole definition; not every manipulated image qualifies. The bill states criminal-publication exceptions for authorized investigative/protective/intelligence activity, reasonable good-faith legal/reporting/medical/scientific/education/help-seeking disclosures, disclosures reasonably intended to assist the person, self-depictions and the identified child-abuse/obscene-material categories subject to other law. Adult publication offenses have a two-year maximum imprisonment and minor offenses three years, with fines; authentic-image threats use those penalties, while digital-forgery threats have distinct18/30-month maxima. The printed threat purposes, forfeiture and restitution provisions remain. Restitution follows18USC2264 and can include court-determined medical/therapy, housing, child-care, lost-income and other covered losses; a mandatory order is not proof of collection. Separately, within one year after enactment covered platforms must establish a clear notice/removal process. A valid written request requires signature, locating information, a good-faith nonconsent statement and contact information; removal is due as soon as possible and within 48 hours, with reasonable efforts to remove known identical copies. The liability protection covers good-faith disabling/removal based on facts or circumstances making unlawful publication apparent, even if the depiction is ultimately determined not unlawful. FTC enforcement treats failure to reasonably comply as the specified unfair/deceptive rule violation and expressly extends to covered nonprofit organizations. Platform coverage includes public user-content forums or services regularly publishing/hosting the identified material, with the printed broadband, email and qualified preselected-content exclusions. Severability and other-law savings remain.

H.R.1223 would require the NSF Director, consulting the named federal vessel owners and university/laboratory owners or operators, to submit an 18-month plan for cybersecurity and telecommunications of the U.S. Academic Research Fleet. The plan must assess scientific-mission network needs, cybersecurity needs in accordance with the named CISA/NIST guidance, additional equipment/personnel/charter-rate costs, implementation timing under varying budgets, common solutions/licensing/centralization and a spending plan developed with non-Federal vessel owners. As appropriate, planning considers operational communications; telemedicine, mental-health care/counseling/crisis support; scientific/cloud/disaster-recovery data; remote maintenance and science participation; and educational outreach. Security considerations include the named2021 JASON recommendations as applied to this fleet, international guidance, personnel/training and controlled/classified information requirements. The Director may support coordinated cyberinfrastructure/security upgrades consistent with the plan and must report progress within two years after plan submission. The fleet is limited to United States-flagged research-university/laboratory vessels meeting the bill's research-vessel, evaluation/designation and active UNOLS-participation predicates.

H.R.2035 would create a DOT-specific exception to the existing55305(a) government-cargo framework: where DOT procures, contracts for or obtains equipment/materials/commodities for its own account, or provides the specified federal financing or advances funds/credits for furnishing or obtaining them, the Secretary or financing recipient must take necessary and practicable steps to place100percent of ocean-carried gross tonnage on eligible privately owned U.S. commercial vessels. Tonnage is computed separately for dry bulk carriers, dry cargo liners and tankers. The requirement applies to the extent such vessels are available at fair and reasonable U.S.-commercial-vessel rates, with fair and reasonable geographic participation. The existing general(a) minimum is at least50percent; the bill inserts the DOT exception and redesignates existing(c)-(f) as(d)-(g), rather than raising every civilian agency's cargo share. Existing(b) vessel eligibility remains incorporated: ordinarily at least three years of U.S. documentation, with the separately specified post-January1,2030 agreement route for vessels documented for less than three years. Existing emergency-waiver and program-administration provisions are retained under the redesignation.

H.R.1709 would require the Assistant Secretary of Commerce for Communications and Information, consulting DHS, to submit a report within one year after enactment to the named House and Senate commerce committees. It would assess how mobile providers have addressed identified vulnerabilities; customer risk/price choices and evaluation tools; best practices; encryption/authentication use, efficacy and adoption barriers; legitimate-network authentication; and adversaries' surveillance/interception technologies such as cell-site simulators. The consultation list applies to the degree practicable and includes public agencies, researchers, standards participants, international stakeholders as coordinated with State, providers including small/rural providers, manufacturers and other experts. The report is limited to mobile service networks, excludes5G protocols/networks, limits the(b)(1) assessment to vulnerabilities shown exploited outside laboratories or feasibly/practicably exploitable in real-world conditions, and considers effectively mitigated vulnerabilities. It is unclassified with a possible classified annex; potentially exploitable unclassified information must be redacted, with an unredacted version supplied to the committees. The bill's U.S.-customer scope covers the incorporated commercial mobile or commercial mobile data service definitions; its adversary definition is not limited to foreign governments.

H.R.1770 would require CPSC to establish an AI pilot within one year after enactment in support of its existing consumer-product-safety mission. The pilot must use AI for at least one of four tasks: injury trends, product hazards, retail/internet sales of recalled new or used products, or identification of products required refused at importation under2066(a). Consultation with specified technical, cybersecurity, retail/manufacturer, product-safety and other participants must be consistent with2055. A public congressional report is due within one year after the pilot concludes; the bill does not set a fixed pilot duration. Commerce must complete a blockchain consumer-protection study within one year after enactment, examining uses, investment, partnerships, benefits/risks, possible regulatory modifications and recommendations, with opportunity for public comment/advice. A public congressional report follows within six months after study completion. Separately, FTC must report within one year after enactment on its token-related unfair/deceptive-practice actions, other prevention efforts and legislative recommendations. A token uses the bill's transferable digital-representation definition. Existing consumer-product coverage, CPSC mission/disclosure controls and FTC unfair/deceptive-practice authority are incorporated references, not new universal product or financial jurisdiction.

H.R.1717 would require FCC within 90 days after enactment either to establish a council advising on communications-network security, reliability and interoperability, or designate an operating advisory committee chartered for those purposes and adjust its membership if needed. The Chair appoints members; to the extent practicable the council includes trusted communications-industry and public-interest/academic representatives and federal, State, local and Tribal governments, with at least one representative of each government type. Members need relevant knowledge/experience; terms are two years, vacancies fill the remainder, and members may remain until successors take office. Every two years after establishment/designation, the council submits its and working groups' adopted reports from the preceding two-year period, including relevant recommendations; FCC must publish submitted reports. The bill exempts the council only from5USC1013(a)(2) advisory-committee termination. Not-trusted status follows a public Chair determination of foreign-adversary ownership/control/influence, or a Chair national-security-threat determination using the named1601(c)(1)-(4) categories as appropriate.

H.R.3062 would require a certificate of crossing for constructing, connecting, operating or maintaining the defined border-crossing portion of an oil/natural-gas pipeline or electric transmission facility importing/exporting oil or gas or transmitting electricity across an international border of the United States, subject to the printed exclusions. That portion is within1,000feet of the international boundary measured from its crossing into the United States. Within120days after final action under NEPA, FERC for pipelines or the Energy Secretary for electric facilities would issue the certificate unless finding the work inconsistent with the public interest. Electric certificates require compliance with applicable Electric Reliability Organization/regional-entity and RTO/ISO policies and standards. Exclusions cover facilities operating at enactment, already permitted facilities, and pending permit applications until the earlier of denial or two years after enactment if not issued, retaining the printed enactment-date qualification. The certificate does not displace the bill's expressly retained federal statutes, NGA sections3/7 or oil-pipeline rate regulation. The bill adds a30day decision requirement after a complete NGA3(c) application for import/export natural gas involving Canada or Mexico; existing3(c) treats qualifying free-trade-agreement gas as public-interest consistent and grants applications without modification or delay. It repeals FPA202(e)'s electric-export order requirement, removes the linked State-regulation restriction, and changes the seasonal-diversity electricity-exchange hearing/finding clause to the Energy Secretary. The replacement finding uses the printed OR between not impairing U.S. electric supply and not impeding public-interest coordination; it is not silently changed to AND. No Presidential or similar permit would be required for covered pipelines/transmission facilities, and specified existing-project modifications would require neither such permit nor a crossing certificate. Modification includes reverse flow, ownership, volume, interconnection and adjustments to maintain flow, such as reducing or increasing pump/compressor stations, as printed. The President could not revoke covered permits issued under the named or any other executive order unless Congress authorizes revocation. Subsections(a)-(e), including their amendments, take effect one year after enactment; that delayed clause does not include(f)'s revocation restriction. Relevant agencies must propose rules within180days and finalize within one year. Yea/Nay concern this whole passage choice, not a permit decision on a named project.

H.R.1608 would require the Homeland Security Secretary, coordinated with TSA and CISA, to report to the specified House Homeland Security and Senate Commerce/Homeland Security committees within180days after enactment. Required subjects include current/emerging vehicular-terrorism threats, connected/autonomous vehicles, driver-assistance systems, ride-sharing, AI/machine-learning and associated technologies; higher-risk locations including transportation hubs, government facilities, power plants, oil refineries, healthcare facilities and crowds; existing research and actions involving barriers, bollards, geofencing, surveillance/cybersecurity and response; private-sector collaboration, threat-sharing and training; recommendations concerning vehicle immobilization/remote-disable technologies, predictive/AI analytics and cybersecurity against misuse of connected/autonomous/driver-assisted vehicles; privacy, civil-rights and civil-liberties stakeholder engagement; and public-awareness initiatives including smaller jurisdictions. These are report elements and recommendations, not new statutory requirements to deploy surveillance, disable vehicles or purchase technology. The report is classified but may include an unclassified executive summary; that summary, if included, must be published on DHS's publicly accessible website. A briefing is due within30days after submission. Vehicular terrorism means use of an automotive vehicle to commit terrorism as defined in6USC101(18), whose dangerous/destructive, criminal-law and apparent-intent conditions remain material. The bill's findings are Congress's statements; this candidate does not independently establish an incident, actor's motive, technology effectiveness or future danger.

H.R.2659 would require DHS acting through CISA, consulting the Attorney General, FBI and appropriate Sector Risk Management Agencies, to establish a joint task force within120days after enactment. Its purpose is collaboration/coordination among agencies assigned federal roles under NSM22 of April30,2024 or a successor to detect, analyze and respond to the specified PRC state-sponsored cyber threats, including the bill-defined Volt Typhoon. CISA or its designee chairs and FBI or its designee vice-chairs; appropriate agency representatives should have the specified expertise, vacancies use the original appointment process, and the task force may coordinate with existing efforts to avoid redundancy. An initial report is due540days after establishment; an annual report is due not later than one year after the initial report and annually thereafter for five years, preserving that printed sequence rather than silently collapsing it to a chosen total. Contents include sector risks/trends/tactics, additional resources/authorities, classified crisis/conflict assessments of infrastructure disruption, U.S. countermeasures, military mobility and economic/social ramifications, recommendations, and a one-time owner/operator awareness-campaign plan. Classified congressional briefings follow each report within30days. Reports are classified, with optional unclassified executive summaries that must be public if included. Named officials must provide information the task force considers necessary, but receipt/handling/storage/dissemination remain subject to applicable law and executive orders, and classified access requires appropriate clearances. The bill exempts the task force from all of5USCchapter10(FACA) and44USCchapter35(Paperwork Reduction Act), distinct from a narrow duration-only exemption. The termination clause prints60days after the final briefing required by subsection(h)(4), although briefings are in(f)(4) and(h)has no(4); this candidate retains that unresolved drafting reference and does not manufacture a precise termination date. Definitions retain the bill's applicable agencies, critical infrastructure, cybersecurity-threat and intelligence-community boundaries. The retained advisory identity pages verify the named document, not every technical claim or predicted conflict outcome.

H.R.2683 would add remote access to ECRA's control, licensing, administration, compliance, penalty, enforcement and coordination framework. New4801(15) covers purposeful, knowing, reckless OR negligent access to a U.S.-jurisdiction item under the Act by a foreign person through a network, including internet/cloud services, from a location other than the item's physical location IF Commerce determines that its use could pose a SERIOUS national-security or foreign-policy risk. Items include commodities, software and technology. This is not a universal overseas, China, AI-model, internet or cloud-access ban and supplies no specific new controlled-item/country/model list. Existing4801(5) excludes citizens, lawful permanent residents and other1324b(a)(3)protected individuals from the natural-person foreign category. That imported definition includes nationals and specified lawful temporary residents, refugees and asylees with its naturalization qualifications; the separately explicit LPR route is not erased by qualifications on another route. The entity branch is separate, and4801(13)U.S.person includes any person in the United States; these categories are not simple complements. Provider duties can apply without a provider being the foreign recipient. No unrestricted access entitlement or immigration/employment status change follows. The bill adds defined remote access to the President's shall-control and shall-regulate duties, Commerce's controlled-item/person/end-use lists, prohibition on UNAUTHORIZED transfers, license/conditions/suspension/revocation, foreign-availability assessment, information/compliance, item/conveyance inspection/seizure/temporary denial, monitoring, license-required notice and specified enhanced controls. Regulations/licensing apply within the existing framework; the statute is not an automatic denial of every foreign person's access. Retained4813(b)incorporates qualified IEEPA1702(b) personal-communication, humanitarian-donation, informational-material and travel limits, including their printed determinations/exceptions, not a blanket software/model exemption. Existing enhanced controls retain material-contribution denial standards and other-agency authorization exceptions. Administration/person-list/end-use monitoring, licensing, compliance assistance, confidentiality and interagency coordination extend to remote access as specified. Existing licensing transparency and no-fee provisions remain; thirty-day processing is a sense-of-Congress BEST-EFFORTS standard, not a hard deadline or automatic license. Commerce must keep House Foreign Affairs and Senate Banking fully/currently informed of anticipated remote-access regulations, risk, regulatory method and economic impact, classified as necessary; their approval is expressly NOT a prerequisite. The remote-access definition expressly does not lower criminal mens rea: retained4819(b)willful violations/attempts/conspiracies or aiding/abetting retain statutory maxima of$1million and20years for individuals as printed, not new strict-liability imprisonment for negligence or current inflation-adjusted civil pricing. Civil fines/license revocation/access prohibitions retain notice/opportunity for agency hearing. The prior-conviction bar is discretionary, covers any item whether controlled or not, for up to10years, and related-party extensions require a shown relationship and retained hearing procedures. The prior-conviction authority also permits revocation of interested licenses/authorizations, extended as printed to provision of remote access. Existing criminal forfeiture and other administrative/judicial/settlement powers remain distinct. Enforcement/search/detention/seizure concern covered items/conveyances and control violations; no immigration detention/removal power is created by DHS participation. This is one whole suspension-and-passage choice; no component endorsement, license decision, enactment, implementation, individual status or member motive is inferred.

H.R.2189 is the complete two-title package deemed adopted under H.Res.1057 using RCP119-18, then put to final passage. TitleI adds a less-than-lethal projectile-device exception alongside the existing antique-firearm exception in18USC921(a)(3), and adds(39). A qualifying device must satisfy ALL conditions: it is not designed/intended to expel and cannot readily be converted to accept/discharge common handgun/rifle/shotgun ammunition OR any other projectile over500feet per second; is designed/intended for use not likely to cause death or serious bodily injury; and cannot accept or readily be modified to accept feeding devices loaded inside a pistol grip OR commonly used in semiautomatic firearms. A requested Attorney General determination is due90days after receipt of the DEVICE. These are classification criteria, not a finding that every labeled device is harmless or an exception limited to police purchasers. TitleII exempts qualifying devices, devices on the Secretary's separate above500feet-per-second list, and shells/cartridges satisfying the intended-use/injury criterion and designed for those devices, from4181 manufacturer/producer/importer sales excise tax. The ordinary device definition repeats the feature/design limits. A manufacturer/producer/importer classification request has a90day decision clock after receipt of the REQUEST; requests during the initial180days are deemed received at that period's close. The Secretary must publish and annually update both the ordinary qualifying-device list and the separate list that would qualify except for the500feet-per-second condition, with an annual congressional report explaining inclusion/exclusion from the latter. Section203 adds both device categories to5845(a)National Firearms Act definition exclusions. That separate listed-device tax/NFA route does NOT expand TitleI's921(a)(39)definition. The tax amendments apply to articles sold after enactment as printed. Existing military/small-manufacturer/paid-NFA excise exceptions, antique/qualified collector-device NFA exclusions, and119-21section70436's enacted transfer/making-tax and4182(a)changes remain context; no universal prior tax burden or first-ever federal device exemption is asserted. Existing INA237(a)(2)(C)expressly incorporates firearm OR destructive device as defined in921(a); its in-and-admitted chapeau, after-admission CONVICTION, specified conduct and violation-of-law conditions remain. TitleI does not amend921(a)(4)'s separate destructive-device definition, so an exception to the firearm branch does not establish immunity under every route or other law. Existing922(g)(5)firearm/ammunition restrictions distinguish unlawful presence and nonimmigrant-visa admission with retained(y)exceptions/waivers; not all noncitizens have the same predicate. No individual device/conviction classification, adjudication, retroactive immigration relief, State use-of-force change, actual sale/tax saving, enactment or safety effect is inferred. This is one whole-bill choice, not a component endorsement.

S.2503's complete Senate-passed ES was offered February23 and put to the recorded House suspension-and-passage vote February24. The motion FAILED264-133 under the two-thirds requirement despite majority Yea votes; neither this choice nor the earlier voice response establishes House passage or enactment. Section3 would immediately narrow91.225(f)(1)sensitive-government missions, excluding routine, non-classified, proficiency and below-Cabinet/Joint-Chiefs-Chair official flights, with ATC notice when not transmitting and monthly notice of ClassBmissions to named committees. The retained baseline exception already requires FAA authorization and specified defense/homeland-security/intelligence/law-enforcement operational-security/safety conditions; the separate ATC-direction exception is not the same branch. FAA must update regulations and agency agreements within one year, with status reporting if late. Agency attestations beginning within90days and quarterly thereafter/flight lists/classified annexes, FAA180day-then-biannual reports and special notices, a two-year GAO before/after review, FAA continuation determinations for noncompliant operators and annual DOT-IG audits beginning after three years provide distinct oversight, not proof of actual noncompliance. Section4 requires an ADS-B In final rule within two years, effective within60days of publication, with equipage by December31,2031 for aircraft required to have ADS-B Out, excluding unmanned aircraft and retaining ATC authorization. FAA must establish performance requirements for an acceptable alternative-equipment pathway for part 91 aircraft with maximum certificated takeoff weight below 12,500 pounds and qualifying military aircraft specified in consultation with Defense. Eligible operators may use an FAA-acceptable alternative to satisfy the ADS-B In requirement; they are not required to choose alternative equipment. The printed situational-awareness, portable/display, avionics and airworthiness conditions and military briefing duties remain; this is not an unconditional all-aircraft mandate. A qualified in-service operator may request up to one additional year, requiring an acceptable application/progress attestation, significant-disruption determination and no uncorrected specified violations; it is not a blanket extension. A negotiated-rulemaking committee is optional, with consultation required if absent; conditional committee/proposal duties, low-cost alternatives and proactive equipage apply as printed. The rulemaking includes a rebuttable cost-benefit/safety PRESUMPTION, not this candidate's empirical conclusion. Separation-standard proposed rulemaking, FAA order changes and controller training have separate relative clocks; an ACAS-X deployment action plan is mandatory while implementation actions are permissive. ARAC reviews ClassDequipment needs rather than automatically extending the mandate to all ClassDoperations. Section5repeals only FY2026NDAA373(a), applying chapter157as if its amendments had not been enacted; that removes the specified military training-flight proximity-warning limitation/waiver framework in covered DCairspace, not373(b)near-miss reports. Section6requires an Army-IG coordination/training/equipment/maintenance/incident audit initiated within60days, periodic progress briefings, unredacted congressional results and public results subject to national-security redaction. Section7establishes/designates an FAA-DOD coordination office within30days and requires the specified DCreview, risk-prioritized other-airport reviews, consultations, incident analyses and staffing. DC initiation is within30days after office establishment and completion within120days of review initiation; other ClassB/C/Dinitiation deadlines are sequential90day clocks and completion within180days of each initiation. DCresults go to Congress within60days of completion; other results are reported every six months after enactment. Section8requires safety-information-sharing MOUs with Army within60days and Navy/AirForce/CoastGuard within90days, with seven-day congressional notice. Section9DEEMS the May10,2024FAA-DODagreement to be the joint notice under FY2019section1046(b), making1046(a)cease as of that date under the proposal; it does not independently prove the historical notice was submitted. The agreement must be updated consistently with section3regulations and remains subject to joint modification, either Secretary's termination or law. Baseline1046(a)limited ADS-B installation/service/access requirements for fighter/bomber/special-mission aircraft until the specified joint notice. No actual equipment installation, regulation, MOU, appropriation, prevented accident, agency motive or safety outcome is inferred.

H.R. 7084 would add a category to existing 46 USC 70022 restrictions on foreign vessels for which a notice of arrival is required. A covered vessel could not enter or operate in U.S. navigable waters or transfer cargo in a U.S.-jurisdiction port/place, subject to the section's exceptions. The new category is a vessel that transited a port, harbor or marine terminal which, AT THE TIME of transit, was in a Western Hemisphere country with a U.S. free-trade agreement, was accessible only through land owned/held/controlled directly or indirectly by a U.S. person, and had an unremoved Presidential designation. The President MAY designate when the foreign government's agency/official has nationalized or expropriated the described U.S.-person port property, or taken other action effectively doing so to the port or its exclusive-access land. The pending-free-trade-arbitration qualification is printed in designation paragraph (2)(B); this candidate does not silently extend it to every designation branch or adjudicate a dispute. The President SHALL remove a designation if the President determines any printed removal condition is met: designation conditions no longer apply; ownership is restored and seizure measures terminated; adequate/effective full-value convertible-exchange or mutually acceptable compensation is provided as specified; OR the dispute is otherwise resolved to the President's satisfaction. The bill adds limitations for vessels in redesignated (b)(1) when a vessel or individual aboard experiences an emergency, or when the described owner authorizes transit of the defined facilities. Existing (a)(2) State Department determination, notice and publication provisions, including their distinct listed-vessel branches, remain context; they are not converted into a blanket new-country waiver. Existing provisional entry/cargo transfer for vessel/person safety and innocent/transit passage protections remain. No actual expropriation, vessel violation, owner status, designation, compensation, port closure, enactment or member motive is inferred. This is one final-passage choice on the complete EH, not an observed sanction against a named vessel.

H.R. 1681 would require the Assistant Secretary of Commerce for Communications and Information to establish a strike force within 180 days after enactment. Members are the Assistant Secretary, BLM and Forest Service heads, and Agriculture/Interior designees other than the Forest Service Chief/BLM Director. Duties include periodic calls, objective and reasonable review goals, and monitoring/facilitating accountability for agencies and their specified field/regional/management units to prioritize communications-use authorization reviews. The Assistant Secretary must report to the named six House/Senate committees within 270 days after enactment on effectiveness. That is a report deadline, not a new 270-day automatic-approval rule for each application. Communications use means facility placement/operation; authorization means an agency easement, right-of-way, lease, license or other authorization to locate/modify a facility on covered land primarily for its communications occupancy/use. The incorporated 47 USC 1455(d) facility definition includes licensed/permitted wireless or wireline transmission infrastructure and the specified fixed-location authorized antenna/apparatus. Covered land is defined public lands and National Forest System land, not every federal parcel: the retained BLM public-land definition excludes Outer Continental Shelf and specified lands held for the benefit of Indigenous peoples; 16 USC 1609(a) identifies the forest/range/related lands, grasslands and other Forest Service administered/designated areas. The measure creates coordination, prioritization, goals and accountability; it does not itself grant an authorization, waive environmental law, mandate a deployed broadband connection or establish a member's preferred individual project. Whole suspension-and-passage support/opposition does not establish enactment or a connectivity outcome.

H.R. 5200 would require at least one FCC public hearing within one year after enactment and annually thereafter relating to ALL preceding-year events for which the Disaster Information Reporting System was activated for at least seven days. FCC must CONSIDER including the listed affected government/resident/consumer, provider, academic, utility, infrastructure and responder representatives; that is not a guaranteed seat for every category or a separate hearing per event. Within 120 days after each hearing concludes, FCC must issue a report on the number/duration of specified broadband, interconnected VoIP, mobile and mobile-data outages; approximate users/infrastructure potentially affected; outages preventing emergency centers from receiving caller location/number, receiving calls and routing them to responders; and resiliency recommendations. These items are required to the extent KNOWN WITHOUT collecting additional information; FCC must consider collected event/System/hearing information. Reports are published on FCC's website upon issuance, excluding information exempt under FCC rules or submitted with a proper confidentiality request under the cited rule. A separate investigation and public report within one year must examine visual outage-notification information's value to public-safety agencies, potentially unreported 911 outages under existing thresholds, provider burden/practicality and recommended rule changes. Recommendations do not themselves change thresholds or require every provider to supply visual information. Emergency communications centers include the printed designated-receiving-facility/function or public-safety-answering-point branches, covering call analysis, dispatch, transfer, responder communications and incident command. The bill retains its incorporated service/outage/government definitions and expressly does not give FCC or anyone authority over broadband providers beyond this section's specific authorization. No actual outage, company noncompliance, rule adoption, uninterrupted 911 service, rescue, survival, enactment or member motive is inferred.

H.R. 5201 would require FCC to publish a website report within 180 days after enactment on enforcement of 47 USC 623. Required subjects are the extent of manufacturer/vendor compliance, obstacles, possible policy improvements if necessary, and possible legislative recommendations if necessary. The existing baseline separately governs manufacture/import/sale/lease and installation/management/operation of multi-line systems in the United States: a user can directly call 911 from an equipped dialing station without an additional digit/code/prefix/postfix, including a trunk-access 9. Existing on-site/other-recipient notification applies when the system can be configured without hardware/software improvement. The retained applicability note concerns systems manufactured/imported/first offered/sold/leased or installed after two years from the 2018 enactment, not a new blanket retroactive duty created by this report bill. Existing State-law and enforcement qualifications remain. The bill imports the existing multi-line-system definition and directs an enforcement/compliance review; it does not amend those underlying duties, guarantee every system's compliance, automatically change FCC policy or enact recommended legislation. No particular manufacturer's violation, actual rescue, coverage, enactment or member motive is inferred from the whole suspension-and-passage choice.

S. 1003 would require FCC to issue an order within 180 days after enactment providing that a shark attack is an event for which an Alert Message MAY be transmitted. The incorporated 47 CFR 10.10(a) definition is an emergency-information message meeting requirements for transmission by a participating commercial mobile service provider under that part. The mandatory duty is FCC's order; the text does not mandate transmission for every attack, require every provider to participate, detect an actual shark, guarantee delivery, establish a beach closure or provide medical treatment. The exact question is House suspension and passage of the Senate-passed ES, not Senate enactment. Yea/Nay describe that whole motion; Present or Not Voting supplies no directional choice. No actual attack, notification, prevented injury, agency compliance or enactment is inferred.

H.R. 3106 would require the Homeland Security Secretary, through appropriate DHS offices/components, to develop and conduct a collective response-to-terrorism exercise, either in addition to OR as part of existing exercise programs. Its scenario must address an extreme-cold event such as a polar vortex and access to critical services; cascading effects on critical infrastructure; mitigation of a successful attack's effects; bolstering affected communities' resilience; coordination with appropriate federal, State, local, Tribal and territorial agencies; and private-sector/community coordination. The incorporated 42 USC 5195c(e) definition covers physical or virtual systems/assets whose incapacity/destruction would have the specified debilitating security, economic-security or public-health/safety impact, not merely a named building or one utility. Within 60 days AFTER COMPLETING the exercise, the Secretary must send the House Homeland Security and Senate Homeland Security/Governmental Affairs committees an after-action report, consistent with protecting classified information, including initial findings, immediate/longer-term plans to incorporate lessons and proposed legislative changes. The bill prints no separate exercise-completion deadline and does not require an independently new standing program. The report is not a public-website mandate, and proposed legislative changes are not enacted by reporting them. No actual attack, weather emergency, infrastructure failure, agency takeover, completed exercise, safety outcome or enactment is inferred from this whole suspension-and-passage choice.

H.R. 8897 would permit, rather than require, the TSA Administrator to establish an airport pilot expediting ACCESS TO security screening for adults and accompanying children twelve or under, subject to the printed no-compromise-of-security condition. If established, TSA must screen each passenger according to that passenger's Secure Flight vetting status under 49 USC 44903(j)(2); screeners under44901 cannot admit ANY passenger to PreCheck or another expedited screening lane without a boarding pass indicating that eligibility. The pilot therefore does not itself give every adult/child PreCheck or an exemption from screening. Existing44901general passenger/property screening and44903(j)(2)preboarding evaluation, selected-passenger/baggage screening, watchlist/privacy/redress safeguards remain context, not new immigration or citizenship criteria. TSA must permit local management to open/close checkpoint lanes and reallocate available resources based on passenger volume to maximize security effectiveness/efficiency. In airport selection TSA must prioritize airports it determines have high volumes of passengers with accompanying children, consider adequate space/personnel while maintaining other lanes' staffing, and use other necessary considerations. If the pilot is established, a briefing to the named House/Senate homeland-security and Senate commerce committees is due within270days AFTER ESTABLISHMENT, and TSA shall carry out the pilot for a period of two years. That clock is not enactment and the duration is not stated as an unconditional permanent program or merely any shorter period TSA chooses. The title's American/family wording does not supply a printed citizenship or legal-parenthood test. No particular airport selection, expanded boarding-pass eligibility, vetting determination, waived security standard, faster actual trip, cost saving or enactment is inferred. This is the whole as-amended suspension-and-passage choice.

H.R. 139 would repeal ALL of15USC260a, including its March-to-November one-hour advancement rule, State-law supersession provision and specific federal enforcement subsection. It would amend261(a)'s nine standard-time offsets: zones1-8 move from UTC minus4/5/6/7/8/9/10/11hours to minus3/4/5/6/7/8/9/10hours, and zone9 from UTC plus10hours to plus11hours. Each printed change advances that statutory offset by one hour; this is not simply renaming the existing seasonal dates. New261(b)offers the printed choice only for a State or area already exempt under260a(a)as in effect the day before enactment: use the amended261(a)standard or the pre-enactment261(a)standard, as the State considers appropriate. It is not an express new option for every State to choose arbitrary times. The existing Uniform Time Act's267definition of State includes the named district/commonwealths/possessions; that definition is for that Act, not a universal definition for unrelated laws. This candidate does not adjudicate a named territory's new option or silently reduce the referenced prior-exemption category to fifty States. Existing261keeps nine zones and DOT's boundary-order role with regard to commerce/common-carrier junction/division points; existing262requires zone time, insofar as practicable as determined by Transportation, for interstate/foreign common-carrier movement and specified federal acts/time limits. The bill changes the standard-time framework used there without rewriting those unaffected clauses. Its conforming change replaces261(a)'s260aexception with the new261(b)exception and redesignates the UTC-definition subsection. No named jurisdiction's current opt-out status, actual clock-change date, zone-boundary order, transportation schedule, health/sleep outcome, enactment or unrestricted State authority is inferred from this final-passage choice.

S. 307 would require BOP, within90days after enactment, to fully implement EACH recommendation in the specifically named2023DOJOIG report23-034. The complete nine-recommendation list calls for queryable DARTS fields identifying victim type/gender and specific inmate behavior; staff training on those fields/codes; consistent policies and data-tracking mechanisms; regular institution/across-BOP risk assessments emphasizing female-staff risks; review of corrective actions from the Coleman/Victorville settlements and assessment of which should extend across institutions; a comprehensive mitigation strategy incorporating appropriate corrective actions and assessment findings; recurring BOP-wide sharing; a training-needs assessment within that strategy; and continuing reporting/prevention/mitigation/resource training. It does not command unassessed universal implementation of every settlement remedy. If implementation is incomplete at the90daydeadline, BOP must report to Congress by that same deadline with explanations and a detailed implementation timeline; this does not replace or erase the full-implementation duty. Within1year AFTER full implementation, DOJ Inspector General must request, and BOP provide, updatedFY2022-2025data on inmate-perpetrated harassment/assault against correctional officers or other BOP employees; IG must analyze and send Congress/Attorney General that analysis and any further recommendations, including adequacy of scope identification and mitigation. The analysis must include punishments as of enactment and use during the preceding5years. Within1year AFTER receiving the analysis the Attorney General must promulgate national prevention/reduction/punishment standards. The incorporated4051definitions identify BOP correctional officers and federal prisoners including the specified vulnerable-person category; sexual assault references10USC920(b/c/d), while harassment is expressly defined in the bill. Incorporating those descriptions does not itself impose military jurisdiction on prisoners or create a new criminal penalty. The findings attribute deficiencies/nonimplementation to the2023report; they are not this candidate's current compliance findings. Current web recommendation-status labels are not evidence of compliance at the action date. This whole House suspension-and-passage choice is not enactment, proof of completed software/training, a particular punishment or an observed reduction in incidents.

H.R. 9436 would replace EVERY2028with2035in section101of divisionJJofPL117-328. Under the complete retained operative baseline, subsection(a), notwithstanding other law EXCEPT(b), treats the named final Atlantic Large Whale Take Reduction Plan rule86FR51970as sufficient to ensure continued federal/State authorizations for American lobster/Jonah crab fisheries comply fully with the Marine Mammal Protection Act and Endangered Species Act from enactment through December31,2028; the bill extends that date to December31,2035. It also moves the linked2028deadlines: NMFS throughout the period must consult States and fishery participants to promote innovation/adoption of gear technologies to implement additional whale protection by the new date; promulgate new consistent regulations taking effect by that date using existing/innovative gear technologies as appropriate; and, in consultation with affected States, submit an annual report to Congress on North Atlantic Right Whale status, actions taken and plans to implement measures expected to not exceed Potential Biological Removal by that date, serious injury/mortality by fishery and country, and the proportion of the American lobster and Jonah crab fisheries transitioned to innovative gear technologies that reduce whale harm. The recipient remains Congress; the operative measure expectation is not exceeding Potential Biological Removal, not attaining a target. H.R. 9436 changes dates only and does not amend that recipient or operator. The literal each-place amendment is not only a new compliance-deeming end date, cancellation of those duties, a promise of compliance or automatic gear adoption. Subsection(b)continues its exception for an emergency rule or action extending/making final an emergency rule in place at the baseline section's enactment affecting those two fisheries. It does not establish an unrestricted ban on all new whale protections. The complete one-page RCP119-40substitute, deemed adopted byHRes1499, matches the EH sections1-2under the disclosed formatting comparison. No detailed meaning of the underlying technical rule, current emergency action, present regulatory/legal status, future catch/revenue, whale outcome, enactment or agency performance is inferred. Yea/Nay concerns final passage of this whole amendment after the failed recommittal motion.

H.R. 1501would insert mining and mineral processing into42USC4370m(6)(A)'s sector list before its residual Council-designated category. Under the complete retained paragraph6baseline, the activity must be in the United States, require federal authorization or environmental review and involve infrastructure construction in a listed sector, plus satisfy one of the alternative pathways: NEPA with likely investment MORE THAN$200million and no abbreviated-process qualification; the specified carbon-dioxide-pipeline programmatic-plan/review pathway; the specified NEPA/Tribal-or-related-sponsor/owned-or-jurisdiction-land pathway; or NEPA and Council judgment that size/complexity benefits from enhanced coordination, including multiple-agency or environmental-impact-statement cases. Existing paragraph6(B)excludes projects under23USC139or33USC2348; the bill does not delete these exclusions or the other qualifying criteria. Section3would prohibit the Council from finalizing, implementing, administering or enforcing the specifically titled September22,2023proposed rule88FR65350, not every mining rule or all environmental laws. That retained proposed text would narrow the mining sector to critical-mineral activities while expanding its listed supply-chain activities to extraction/beneficiation/processing/recycling; its proposed operative definitions and sector text, not inferred future agency action, establish the target. The bill itself adds mining/mineral processing to statute and bars that proposal; it does not guarantee coverage, authorize a particular mine, waive required environmental review, guarantee a faster permit, prove economic/resource outcomes or establish enactment. HRes1499deems the Natural Resources substitute adopted for consideration; this candidate binds the final EH and exact passage question without claiming an independent floor/EH comparison. The failedHJRes1motion on the same day is a separate action.

H.R. 4219would require Interior, acting through the Fish and Wildlife Service Director, to carry out a priority-invasive-species program within/adjacent to Refuge System lands/waters and establish at least one trained early-detection/rapid-response team in EACH Service region. Team duties cover habitat conservation/management and appropriate restoration, prevention/detection/response/management, integrated pest-management techniques/tools, outreach/training/table-top exercises including Incident Command System use, and use of risk assessments/research/innovations/monitoring/evaluation to improve detection/response. Interior must engage the listed federal/State/Tribal/local, nonprofit/nongovernmental and private partners; collaborate in developing consistent taxonomy standards and work with others to implement them among EACH Interior database; and use national/regional standardized reporting platforms, with named systems/examples. This is not a mandate to create a single centralized database or a new software platform from scratch. BOTH identification AND response on adjacent lands/waters are permitted only at the owner's request. On request and as appropriate, Interior MAY provide financial/technical assistance, contracts, grants/cooperative agreements and team-expertise agreements; these are not unconditional private entitlements or authority to disregard the owner-request restriction. Interior must encourage coordination with adjacent owners and State/Tribal agencies. Reports to the named four congressional committees AND public Service website are due2and5years after enactment, summarizing team work and progress toward prevention/detection/control/eradication. The program authorizes$10million for EACHFY2027-2033, rather than making those appropriations. Printed definitions distinguish early detection from rapid response and eradication; priority species depend on specified native-species/habitat/health/economic impacts, and State includesDCandterritories/possessions for this section. No automatic finding about a particular organism, completed deployment, owner consent, eradication, guaranteed savings, funding award or enactment follows from the whole as-amended suspension-and-passage choice. Complete printed floor/EH operative bodies match under the retained formatting comparison.

H.R. 8278would require EACH covered agency within180days after enactment to assess how existing technologies challenge adequate real-time supervision, including as applicable coreITinfrastructure, supervision tools, general-market-risk monitoring and data collection/storage/processing/security. By the same deadline each must assess acquisition/development procurement rules/protocols and identify opportunities to streamline them WITHIN its existing authority, including effects on testing new systems. This is an assessment/identification mandate, not itself a waiver of procurement law or a command to acquire a particular platform. Within18months AFTER completing those assessments, and every5years thereafter, the agencies must coordinate and jointly report to the House Financial Services and Senate Banking committees in a manner that does not pose risk to the integrity/security of agency, regulated-entity or market-participant technologies/systems/capabilities. The report covers, as applicable for each agency, hardware/software/advanced analytics and vendor/in-house/contractor categories; voluntary versus mandatory procurement practices and streamlining; technology-development workforce/recruitment/retention and contractor/third-party risk management; supervised-entity information processes/obstacles; jurisdiction-specific market/technology trends, compliance/risk-management use, data quality/interoperability/standardization and illicit-activity risks; interagency sharing/access barriers; estimated supervised-entity system-modification costs; and future upgrade plans, anticipated timelines/costs/procurement barriers, hiring/training, interagency aspects, transition costs/potential reductions and delegated-examiner relationships. Describing plans or estimated reductions does not require implementing upgrades or establish realized savings. Covered agencies are the Federal Reserve Board, CFPB,FDIC,Treasury includingOCCandFinCEN,FHFAandNCUA, not every federal agency or every financial firm. The bill's findings about outdated systems and risks remain attributed congressional assertions, not independently established current performance. Complete September14as-amended floor/EH bodies match under disclosed formatting comparison; initial call-up/postponement and September15recorded choice remain separate evidence. House suspension/passage is not enactment, an actual procurement/upgrade, a public release mandate, new supervisory jurisdiction or a demonstrated compliance/security/consumer outcome.

Its eligible uses include engine/retrofit technologies for buses,trucks,marine engines,locomotives and specified nonroad equipment, plus verified long-idling reduction; priorities/application/monitoring and federal-mandate-funding restrictions, including the printed State-implementation-plan exception, remain. H.R. 9340would add paragraph22toPURPA111(d), with a standard for a covered large-load customer's rate to recover the FULL,INCREMENTALcost of generation/transmission/distribution upgrades necessary for that load, including if the customer terminates the contract/agreement or ceases buying electricity. The standard also requires customer financial assurances or contributions covering upgrade cost BEFORE the utility makes such an upgrade. A covered customer is a NONRESIDENTIALconsumer that on/after paragraph enactment requests or enters a sale-of-electricity agreement for one or more facilities primarily operatingITinfrastructure and related data-storage/computational systems, with aggregate peak electric demand100MEGAWATTS OR MORE at a SINGLE SITE OR CAMPUS. This is not every household/business, every existing contract or the utility's entire cost base. Material retained2621(a)-(c)requires State ratemaking authorities for utilities they regulate and nonregulated utilities to CONSIDER each standard and determine whether implementation is appropriate, after public notice/hearing, with written findings/evidence and public availability. The baseline expressly permits a determination that implementation is not appropriate and, consistently with State law, permits implementation OR DECLINING implementation; declining an otherwise appropriate standard requires public written reasons. The new bill does not remove that framework or compel universal adoption of its cost/assurance standard. New2622(b)(9)requires commencement or a hearing date within1year and completed consideration/determination within2years after paragraph enactment. New2622(i)exempts the new standard from subsections(b)/(c)for a utility where, before enactment, the State implemented the standard or a comparable one, the relevant authority/utility conducted a proceeding considering it, OR the legislature VOTED ON implementation. A prior vote/proceeding need not be silently recast as prior adoption; the exception is to those timing/failure provisions, not a blanket repeal of all PURPAduties. Conforming2622(c)failure-to-comply and2634prior/pending proceeding references use the new paragraph's enactment date;2634's substantial-conformity requirements remain, not automatic approval of every historical proceeding. Complete retained September15as-amended floor/EH bodies match after the disclosed internal page-furniture removal; the initial/postponed and September16recorded choices remain separate. This whole suspension/passage choice does not establish enactment, a named jurisdiction's determination, an actual customer fee/assurance, recovered stranded cost, electricity-price change, data-center construction or universal legal-currentness of dated baselines.

H.R. 375 would require Interior to partner and collaborate with Agriculture and Hawaii to address the tree disease defined in the bill as Rapid Ohia Death. Interior, through the USGS Director, and the Forest Service Chief, through the Institute of Pacific Islands Forestry, must continue research on its vectors and transmission. Interior, through the Fish and Wildlife Service Director, must continue partnering with Agriculture, Hawaii and local stakeholders to manage ungulates in disease-control areas on federal, State and private land, with private landowners' consent for the private-land work. Agriculture, through the Forest Service Chief, must continue providing financial assistance, including through agreements with Interior, to prevent disease spread and restore Hawaii native forests, and staff/necessary infrastructure funding to the named Institute for disease research. These are the whole bill's printed continuation/collaboration duties; the text does not specify a dollar appropriation, new laboratory construction, particular staffing level, reporting deadline or compulsory private-land access. The bill defines its disease and tree by the named scientific terms; this candidate attributes that definition to the bill rather than independently certifying biological taxonomy, current incidence or agency practice. The word continue does not establish from this vote that agencies were actually performing or funding every activity at the action date. No accomplished research, actual funding award, eradication/restoration, prevented spread, scientific result or enactment is inferred. This exact House motion suspends the rules and passes the complete unamended EH; no independent floor-body comparison is claimed.
